q2_gaps: copular-linking appearance verbs with an NP complement ("looks/sounds/feels/tastes like a paradise"): the instruction set routes *seem / appear* to the epistemic Might/Probably status and routes perception verbs with EVENTIVE complements to perception reports, but never says how "look like NP" is encoded — reifying a `look` event with the Like oblique is an extrapolation

an indefinite NP serving as the STANDARD of a likeness comparison ("like a paradise"): the existential rule mints a witness plus its class atom, which asserts that such a thing exists, although "X looks like a Y" makes no existential commitment to any Y
notes: `Like` is explicitly licensed as the surface-preposition oblique, Experiencer is the right subject role for a stative intransitive, and "now" correctly stays a bare deictic constant with no calendar atoms (no TODAY supplied) and no status atom for the bare simple present.
